# Newsletter Form

A ready-to-ship email-capture block. It owns its own email state, validates the address and runs the loading to success flow. Two layouts: a self-contained card and a single-row inline signup.

```tsx
<NewsletterForm onSubscribe={(email) => subscribe(email)} />
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add newsletter-form
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/newsletter-form/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
"use client"

import { NewsletterForm } from "@/components/ui/newsletter-form"

export function Example() {
  async function subscribe(email: string) {
    await fetch("/api/newsletter", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ email }) })
  }

  return <NewsletterForm onSubscribe={subscribe} />
}
```

## Inline

`variant="inline"` drops the card chrome for a single row, ideal inside a [Footer](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/footer.md) or a hero section.

```tsx
<NewsletterForm variant="inline" action="Subscribe" />
```

## API reference

### NewsletterForm

A self-contained signup composed from [Input](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/input.md) and [Button](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/button.md). Forwards all `<div>` props.

- `variant`: `"card"` (default) or `"inline"`.
- `onSubscribe`: `(email: string) => void | Promise<void>`. Return a promise to keep the spinner up until your request resolves.
- `title`, `description`, `placeholder`, `action`, `fineprint`: override the default copy (card variant). Pass `null` to hide description or fineprint.

## FAQ

### Do I have to manage the email state myself?

No. NewsletterForm is a ready-to-ship block: it owns its own email state, validates the address, and runs the loading then success flow. Drop it in and it works.

### How do I hook it up to my mailing-list API?

Wire `onSubscribe`, which receives the entered email on a valid submit. Return a promise from it to keep the spinner up until your request resolves, then the success panel replaces the form.

### When should I use variant="inline" instead of the card?

Use `variant="inline"` for a single-row signup in a Footer or hero section: it drops the card chrome (border, background, padding) down to just the input and button. The default `card` variant adds a heading, lead, and fine print.

### How do I change the copy or hide parts of the card?

Override `title`, `description`, `placeholder`, `action`, and `fineprint`. Pass `null` to `description` or `fineprint` to hide them entirely.

### Why does the nested Input blend with the card instead of looking filled?

Neither layout paints a fill of its own, so the composed Input takes whatever ground the form sits on instead of a mismatched block. Put it on a filled panel that declares `--surface` and the Input follows that panel. That is the DS surface contract at work.

### Does it honor density?

Yes. Density tunes the card padding, gap, and title size, with `compact` (16px) as the default and `comfortable` (24px) for a roomier card; it also reads a surrounding DensityProvider.

`npx koalaui-cli add newsletter-form` writes `components/ui/newsletter-form/`. Import from `@/components/ui/newsletter-form`:

- Types: `NewsletterFormProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `button`, `form`, `input`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `density`, `tv`
